steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Source analysis is a core skill in OCR J280 — especially for visual and material culture

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Classical sources include literary texts, visual sources (vase paintings, sculpture) and material evidence

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Always consider content, provenance and context when analysing a source

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Literary sources may be biased by genre, purpose or audience

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Q: What three elements should you consider when analysing a source? | Q: Why can a biased source still be useful? | Q: How should you approach a vase painting as a source?

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: Content (what it says or shows), provenance (who created it, when, why), and context (what else was happening). | Bias reveals attitudes, values and cultural assumptions of the author or their society. | Describe what you see first, then analyse significance, and evaluate limitations (artistic conventions may distort reality).

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Start source answers by identifying provenance For visual sources, describe before analysing Use: 'This source is useful because... However, it is limited because...' Cross-reference the source with your own knowledge Ask 'what does this source NOT tell me?'
